references.text: The priest shall examine the wound and declare the person unclean if it appears deeper than the skin—the same principle applies to examining skin diseases.
The priest examines whether the wound appears deeper than the skin and whether the hair has turned white—similar diagnostic criteria for leprosy.
The priest shall examine the wound to see if it is deeper than the skin with white hair—parallel to the examination of scurf on the head or beard.
Continuation of the text about scurf—describing what happens if the wound does not appear deeper than the skin.
Further instructions regarding the examination of scurf on the seventh day—part of the same legal text concerning the diagnosis of scurf.
Summary of the laws concerning leprosy and scurf (נֶתֶק)—confirming that this is part of the regulations for skin diseases.
Reminder to follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy—the priest's role in declaring someone clean or unclean.
